text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- ALL NEWSPAPERS: The Reform Party held its congress on Saturday; Siim Kallas will continue as party leader. The possible merger of the Moderates and Fatherland Union parties was mentioned and welcomed.
- SENUMILEHT: a graduate of the Jarveotsa secondary school in Tallinn cheated the school pupils out of more than 50,000 kroons for a study trip to England; the fraud was uncovered by police.

-The lawyer for retired general Alexander Einseln accused the security police of breaking the law by charging the general with abuse of power. Einseln is accused of having authorised an illegal arms purchase.
-Documents reveal that ex-premier Tiit Vahi was actively involved in the management of the Silmet metal processing plant in Sillamae, although he has denied any participation or share ownership.
